subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw commit to this six-event AI-safety taxonomy and manifest-gated plugin emission API as permanent public plugin contracts?
rationale: The PR creates security-sensitive plugin SDK and manifest surfaces whose taxonomy, trust semantics, compatibility guarantees, and ownership cannot be selected safely by automation.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower contract
options.body: Approve the direction but require a host-bound, fully validated capability and installed-plugin proof before any public SDK or manifest surface lands.

options.title: Keep it internal first
options.body: Land only separately approved internal diagnostic contracts and defer third-party plugin emission until the taxonomy stabilizes.

options.title: Decline the core surface
options.body: Keep detector-specific safety telemetry in plugins or existing diagnostics rather than adding a new core taxonomy and permission model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrower contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction but require a host-bound, fully validated capability and installed-plugin proof before any public SDK or manifest surface lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this owner to the intersecting plugin, diagnostic-event, and security boundaries.
